The Agni-priest of the liberal patron who has trimmed the sacrificial grass,
around whom the sacrifices proceed and the strengths of fame gather— [hear us].

Agni is the Hotṛ-priest for those who are liberal givers, for the dwelling of him who has trimmed the sacrificial grass. To him the sacrifices proceed together, and to him the strengths and the glorious riches come together. 2.

That Agni whom all sacrifices—meaning all sacrificial rites (*yajñāsaḥ*)—approach together and go toward; who, while accomplishing the abundant fame of the sacrificer, are themselves the *vājāsaḥ* (strengths) that reach him; such is Agni. He becomes the *hotṛ*, the invoker of the gods, for the sake of the sacrifice of that *dāsvataḥ* (the giver)—one who performs the offering of oblations and so forth—and of that *vṛktabarhiṣaḥ* (one who has trimmed the sacred grass). *Vṛktabarhiḥ* refers to one by whom many *darbha* blades have been cut (*vṛktāni*). His *kṣayasya* (abode): it is called an *kṣaya* because the fruits that accomplish heaven dwell (*kṣiyanti*) within it. For that sacrificer, he is the invoker. Regarding the words: *dāsvataḥ*: from the root *dā* "to give," with the suffix *asun*. Because the suffix *matup* is udātta on its first syllable, the *t* is substituted for *m*. By the accent of the root, it remains udātta on the first syllable. *kṣayasya*: from the root *kṣi* "to dwell" or "to go. By the rule "in the sense of dwelling," it is udātta on the first syllable. *vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*: from the root *vṛjī* "to exclude" or "to avoid"; here, by metaphorical usage, it means cutting. It is a past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*), udātta on the final syllable by the accent of the suffix. Being a *bahuvrīhi* compound, it retains the original accent of the first member. *yajñāsaḥ*: the word *yajña* ends in the suffix *naṅ* according to the rule "yajayāca... and is udātta on the final syllable. *caranti*: from the root *cara* "to move" or "to eat. The suffixes of the present tense (*lasārvadhātuka*) are anudātta because the root is taught with a short *a*. There is no elision of the accent (*nighāta*) because of the rule "after a word ending in *yat* [or *yad*], there is no suppression of the verb's accent. *vājāsaḥ*: from the root *vaj* with the suffix *ghañ*. *Vāja* is udātta on the final syllable by the rule "karṣāvataḥ. This is due to Vedic usage (*chāndasatvāt*).

1. Due to the *ca-ṇa* suffix, there is the acute accent (*udātta*). 2. [The word] begins with the acute accent when preceded by *kha, ca, jha, ṇa, na, bha*, etc. 3. In *kha, ca, jha, ṇa, na, bha, ra, śa*, the word "in succession" (*ānuṣak*) does not exist. 4. [The word belongs to those ending in] *kha, ca, jha, ṇa, bha, ra*, and *vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*. 5. [The word belongs to those ending in] *ga, gha, ca*. 6. [The word] has the acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*) when it is followed by *kha, jha, ta*. 7. [The word] is also [included] due to figurative usage (*upacāra*), according to *kha, ca*. 8. [The word] ends with the acute accent (*antodātta*), according to *kha, ca, jha, ṇa, na, bha, śa*.

In the word *ādityādinethyam*, the accent is udātta on the first syllable. Regarding *śravasyavaḥ*: the suffix *kyac* is applied according to the rule *chandasi parecchāyām*; then the suffix *u* is applied according to the rule *kyācchandasi*. By the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*), it is udātta on the final syllable.
And him whom the kindling-stick has brought forth like a newborn infant,
Agni, the sustainer of the human tribes, the performer of the perfect sacrifice.
And indeed, him whom the two kindling-sticks have brought forth like a newborn infant, Agni, the sustainer of the human tribes, the performer of the excellent sacrifice. 3.

And indeed, [the two fire-sticks] gave birth to that Agni—who is the sustainer of the human tribes (*viś*), who is born from the mind, who is a performer of beautiful sacrifices (*svadhvara*), and who nourishes the bodily constituents through the digestion of food—just as one gives birth to a newborn infant (*śiśu*). The meaning is that the two fire-sticks (*araṇī*) produced this Agni for the sake of nourishing living beings. Regarding the word *śiśum*: from the root *śo* (meaning "to thin" or "to sharpen"), the vowel substitution *ā* occurs according to the rule *ādeca upadeśe'śiti*. The suffix *u* is added with the augment *san*, and there is the state of being *san*. There is reduplication of the root and shortening of the vowel. By the rule *sanyataḥ*, the vowel *i* is substituted. By the rule *bhāto dhātoḥ*, the final *ā* is elided. It is accented on the first syllable because it ends in *ni*. As for *yathā*, by the rule *yatheti pādānte*, it is entirely unaccented. Regarding *janiṣṭa*: from the root *janī* (meaning "to be born"), the *luṅ* (aorist) tense is used. Due to the Vedic character, there is a transposition of the number (person). Regarding *araṇī*: from the root *ṛ* (meaning "to go"), the suffix *ani* is added according to the rule *atisṛbhṛñ-dhmyasyavitṛbhyo'niḥ*. It is accented on the first syllable. Fire goes toward these two; thus they are called *araṇī*. How is the suffix *ani* derived here in the sense of the ablative? It is established by the inclusion in the *bhīmādi* group, despite the restriction in Pāṇini 3.4.75: *tābhyāmanyatronādayaḥ*. Regarding *mānuṣīṇām*: the suffix *an* is added to *manu* with the augment *vuk* by the rule *manojātāvayavato vukca*. The accent falls on the first syllable by the rule *dityadityādityapatyuttarapadāṇṇyaḥ*. Regarding *viśām*: from the root *viś* (meaning "to enter"), the suffix *kvip* is added in the sense of the agent. The case ending is accented by the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. Regarding *svadhvaram*: from the root *dhvara* (meaning "to injure"), the suffix *ac* is added by the rule *pacādyac*. An *adhvara* is that in which there is no injury (*dhvara*) to the sacrifice. By the rule *nañsubhyām*, it is accented on the final syllable as an exception to the general rule for *bahuvrīhi* compounds.
And indeed, you are feared even in difficult places, like a son [hidden] within logs of wood; you who burn many forests, like a beast for the sake of fodder.
And indeed, you are difficult to approach like a son among the logs of wood; you, O Agni, who burn many forests, are like a beast for the pasture. 4.
Moreover, like the son of snakes that move crookedly through wood—
or rather,
like the son of horses that move in curved paths by means of specific gaits such as the *āskandita*— you are seized with difficulty, like an untrained young snake or a child.
O Agni, you who are many, you are the burner of numerous forests;
how so? Like a beast upon pasture grass—that is, like a beast [consuming] grass.
This is the meaning:

just as an animal, extremely afflicted by hunger, when released into a field of grass, devours everything; [as does one who approaches] this fire. (Note: Variant readings include *cainam agnim* and *cavam agnim*.)
2. There is elision of the vowel *a* in the word *ta*.
The suffix *ṇi* is applied when denoting grain (*dhānya*).
From this sūtra, the [suffix] *iti* and others are carried over.

3. A word ending in a suffix beginning with *kha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, or *bha* has its final syllable udātta; likewise for those ending in a suffix beginning with *jha*, *ta*, *ra*, or *ni*; and for those ending in a suffix beginning with *na* or *ni*. 4. Words ending in *pa*, *pha*, *ba*, or *śa* are puruṇi.

The meaning is "he goes toward that. [In the word *durgabhīyase*: the root *bhī* is used in the sense of "seizing" (*upādāne*). The suffix *yak* is added. With the rule "*bhuva īṭ*" still in force, the augment *īṭ* is added by the rule "*bahulaṃ chandasi*. There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule "*prahijyādi-*. The letter *bh* is substituted for *h* by the rule "*hramehabhaśchandasi*. It is subject to the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent. [In the word *haryāṇām*: the root *hṛ* is used in the sense of "crookedness" (*kauṭilye*). The suffix *yat* is added by the rule "*ṛhaloḥ yata*. There is vṛddhi of the first vowel. It receives the *svarita* accent by the rule "*tisvaritam*. [In the word *guru*: the root *pṛ* is used in the senses of "protecting" and "filling. The suffix *ku* is added by the rule "*pṛbhidivyadhigṛdhṛṣṭṛviśibhyaḥ kuḥ*. There is the substitution of *u* for the vowel preceding an *oṣṭhya* sound by the rule "*udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*. It has an udātta accent on the final syllable by the accent of the suffix. [In the word *asi*: there is no *nighāta* because of the rule "*yadvṛttānnityam*."
Half of whose flames, when they are fully joined, go forth smoking;
when Trita blows upon him in heaven, he sharpens him like a smith.
Half of him is for worship; together they go toward him with smoke. When Trita blows upon him in heaven like a smelter, he sharpens him as a smelter does. 5.

And furthermore, when the fire is smoky—that is, possessed of smoke—its flames (*arcayaḥ*) come together beautifully from all sides, reaching everywhere. *Trita* is so called because it is spread across three places, or because it transcends those three places: namely, in heaven and in the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*). When this very self (*ātmānam*) blows upon itself—that is, when it causes itself to increase—the meaning is that the flames then issue forth from all sides.
How is this? Just as a smith (*dhamātā*), by means of bellows and other tools, increases the fire, so too does [the fire] increase its own self. This is the meaning.
Furthermore, "as in the case of the bellower":
just as fire existing near a bellower, being blown by him, sharpens itself—that is, makes itself intense—in the same way, it means that he himself sharpens his own self.
The word "aha" is for the purpose of completing the meter.
They go; [this is from] the root *iṇ* in the sense of "going.
Due to its connection with the word *yat*, there is an absence of the augment *nighāta*.
He blows.
The root *dhmā* means "sound" and "contact with fire.
There is a substitution of *dhma* for [the root *dham*] when preceded by *pātra* and other such words.
As before, there is an absence of *nighāta* (anudātta accent). [The form] *śiśīte* [is derived from] the root *śo*, meaning "to sharpen" (*tanūkaraṇe*).
It is conjugated in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).

While the rule *ślau* is being carried over, the elision (*ślu*) of the verbal suffix occurs according to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. Then, by the rule *ādeca upadeśe śiti*, the substitution of *ā* takes place.
The word *ślau* indicates the state of reduplication (*dvirvacana*).
By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) is shortened.
When the designation *abhyasta* (repeated) is applied by the rule *ubhe abhyastam*, the substitution of *ī* for the final *ā* occurs by the rule *āta: ī halyaghoḥ*.
Because it follows a verbal suffix (tiṅ), there is an absence of the threefold destruction.
Through your protections, O Aharmagha, and through the praises of Mitra,
may we overcome the evils and the enmities of mortal men.
Through your protections and through the praises of Mitra, may we, driven away from hatred, overcome the misfortunes of mortals. 6.

O Agni, through your protections—your acts of preservation performed by you—and through your praises—the hymns of praise offered by us—for the sake of me, who am a friend to all, [may there be safety] from the misfortunes (*duritāni*) of mortal men who have become our enemies; that is, from the instruments of evil wrought by them.

1. By means of *na*, *ra*, *pra-hi*, etc.; by means of *śa*, *pra-hi*, *jyā*, etc. 2. [Words] ending in *kha*, *ca*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha* are udātta (accented) at the end. 3. *Jha* and *ra* undergo augmentation (*upavardhate*). 4. Like *na*, *ra*, and *ś*; like a blacksmith (*dhamātṛ*) and his bellows. 5. *Ta* [is used] for the blacksmith (*dhmātṛ*) in proximity. 6. When *kha*, *ca*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *ra* follow. 7. *Pa*, *pha*, *ba*: [the protection] of Mitra is there through praises (*uti*) and protections (*rakṣāmi*). 8. *Na*, *pa*, *pha*, *ba*: through eulogies (*praśasti*). 9. And with hymns of praise (*stuti*).

"May we, joined with those who hate, cross over [our enemies]—those joined with hatred, as if they were foes. This is the meaning: by means of our own skillful actions and praises unconnected with [worldly] things, may we cross over external and internal enemies. *Ūtibhiḥ*: from the root *ava* in the sense of "to protect," with the suffix *kin*. By the rule *jvaratvara-srivyavimavām upadhāyāśca*, the vowel *ū* is substituted for the radical vowel and the penultimate vowel. It is prescribed as having an udātta accent on the final syllable by the rule *ūti-yūti-jūti-sāti-heti-kīrtayaśca*. *Praśastibhiḥ*: from the root *śaṃsu* in the sense of "to praise," with the suffix *kin*. Because it is a *kṛt* compound where the second member retains its original accent (*kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svara*), the prefix *pra-* retains its original accent by the rule *tādau ca niti kṛtyatau*. *Dveṣayutaḥ*: from the root *dvip* in the sense of "displeasure," with the suffix *asun* in the abstract sense (*bhāve*). From the root *yu* in the sense of "mixing," with the suffix *kvip* in the agentive sense (*kartari*), followed by the augment *tuk*. It retains the accent of the second member of the *kṛt* compound. *Turyāma*: from the root *tṛ* in the senses of "floating" and "crossing," used in the optative (*liṅ*) for a prayer. The suffix *yāsuṭ* is added; the *s* is elided by the rule *liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya*. The *śap* is elided by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. The *u* is substituted for the vowel before the labial by the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya bahulaṃ chandasi*. Since the *yāsuṭ* augment is udātta, the remaining syllables are anudātta (*śeṣanighāta*). There is no suppression of the accent (*nighātābhāva*) because of the prohibition *apādādau*.

O Agni, bring that wealth to us, O powerful one, for the sake of our two heroes. May he be the one who bestows long life and prosperity; may he be the winner of the prize of straightness. And do thou stand by us for our increase in battles.

O Agni, bring that wealth toward us; O powerful one, bring it to the men. May he cause us to dwell securely, may he cause us to prosper; may he be for the winning of booty. And be present for our increase in battles. 7.

O Agni, O powerful and mighty one, you who are the leader of our oblations, bring toward us—that wealth which is renowned in this world, that treasure characterized by the path—bring it here, present it before us. May that aforementioned Agni drive away; may he drive away our enemies. May that Agni nourish; may he nourish us. May he be for the sake of the acquisition (*sātaye*) of *vāja*, that is, food. And furthermore, O Agni, in battles, in conflicts, be eager for our prosperity (*vṛdhe*); in the struggle, for the sake of victory over the enemy, may you bring about our success—this is the meaning. *Sahasvaḥ*: from the root *paha* (in the sense of enduring). With the suffix *asun*. "That by which enemies are endured" is *sahaḥ*, meaning strength. The possessive suffix *matup*. By the rule *mādupadhāyāḥ*, there is the substitution of *v* for *m*. By the rule *matuvaso ruḥ saṃbuddhau chandasi*, there is the substitution of *r* in the vocative in the Vedic language. There is the *nighāta* accent by the rule *āmantritasya ca*. *Kṣepayat*: from the root *kṣipa* (in the sense of impelling). From the causative (*ṇijanta*), in the *leṭ* mood. Elision of the *i* by the rule *itaśca lopaḥ*. The augment *aṭ* is added by the rule *leṭo'ḍāṭau*. The *śap* suffix, the *guṇa* and *āyādeśa* substitutions, and the substitution of the single substitute (*pararūpatva*). *Poṣayat*: from the root *puṣ* (in the sense of nourishing). *Bhuvat*: from the root *bhū* (in the sense of existence). By the rule *bhūsuvostiṅi*, there is a prohibition of *guṇa*. The substitution of *uvaṅ*. *Edhi*: from the root *as* (in the sense of being). By the rule *dhvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaśca*, [the substitution of *e* occurs]. Because that [substitution] is considered non-existent (*asiddha*), the substitution of *dhi* for *hi* occurs by the rule *hujhalbhyo hedhiḥ*. There is the *nighāta* accent. *Pṛtsu*: by the rule *padādiṣu*, etc., there is the substitution of *pṛt* for the word *pṛtanā*. "agna ojiṣṭham" is the tenth hymn, consisting of seven verses.
The seer and other details, as well as the ritual application (viniyoga), are as before.
The fourth and seventh verses are *paṅkti* meters.
"O Agni, most powerful one, [and] the fourth [verse]," thus it is enumerated.

1. In *pa-pha-ba*, [the suffix] *ahaṃ* is acute on the fourth syllable (*turyāma tareyam*). 2. In *ra*, it is acute on the final syllable (*antodāttatve*); in *śa*, it is acute on the final syllable (*antodāttaḥ*). 3. In *śa*, there is acute accent (*udāttatvam*). 4. In *kha-ca-jha-ṇa-na-bha-ra-śa*, the suffixes are *netāraḥ*. 5. In *kha-ca-ṇa*, [the suffix] is *sānekācaḥ*. 6. In *pa-pha-ba*, the seer is Ātreya Gaya. The fourth and seventh verses are *paṅkti*; the remaining verses are *anuṣṭubh*. The deity is Agni.

O Agni, bring us the most powerful splendor, O Adhigu! Open for us a path toward wealth and abundant nourishment, that we may attain strength. O Agni, bring to us the most powerful splendor, O Adhigu! Open for us a path toward wealth and abundant nourishment, that we may attain strength.

O Agni, bring—that is, bestow upon us—the most powerful (*ojiṣṭham*), most excellent (*balavattamam*) *dyumnam*. *Dyumnam* is wealth, for it shines (*dyotate*) everywhere in the form of bracelets, crowns, and so forth. O *adhiga*, one whose movement (*gamanam*) is unobstructed (*aṣṭamapratihatam*), or one whose rays (*gāvaḥ*) are unrestrained (*aṣṭatā*). Thus he is called *aṣṭaguḥ*.
O Adhigu!
Addressing him thus: "Unite us with *parīṇas*, that is, with wealth (*rāyas*) that is pervasive on all sides, in an excellent manner."

For the sake of vigor (*vāja*) and for the attainment of food (*annābhāya*), fashion (*ratsi*)— that is, carve out or prepare— the path, the very road that is the means for reaching my presence. [Make it] most powerful (*ojiṣṭham*).
The root *ubj* means "straightness.
According to the rule *ubjer bale balopaś ca*, the suffix *asun* is applied with the elision of the syllable *bal*;
there is also *guṇa* [vṛddhi] substitution.
*Ojas*.
In the sense of "that which possesses this," the suffix *vini* is applied according to the rule beginning with *asyāmedhā*;
then, by the rule *atiśāyane*, the suffix *iṣṭhan* is added.
There is elision of the matup suffix.
By the rule "ṭeḥ," there is elision of the final syllable.
It is udātta-accented on the first syllable because it begins with the prefix nis.

*Dyumna*: from the verbal root *dyut* in the sense of "shining" (*dīptau*), the suffix *na* is applied according to the rule *sumnadyumninam*, etc., and the substitution of the letter *m* at the end of the stem is prescribed as a nipātana (irregular formation). It is udātta on the final syllable by the accent of the suffix.
In *adhigo*, the word *agha* is substituted for *aṣṭan*;
the word *go* undergoes shortening as an upasarjana.
The vocative case ending receives the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent. Regarding *parīṇasā*: [the root] *ṇas* is used in the sense of "crookedness" (*kauṭilye*).

In this context, the meaning is "pervasion" (*vyāpti*), because verbal roots have multiple meanings. From this [root], the suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) according to the rule beginning with *saṃpadādi*.
That which has pervasion reaching us is thus described.

The substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*] occurs by the rule "upasargādasamāse’pi" (Pāṇini 8.4.14). However, in this case, because the word *pareṇa* is not joined with the action of leading (*prāpaṇa*), it does not possess the designation of a prefix (*upasarga*) in relation to that action. This is according to the principle: "The designations of motion (*gati*) and prefix (*upasarga*) apply only with respect to that action with which they are connected" (Pāṇini 1.4.60). Therefore, how can there be the substitution of *ṇ*?
In that case, by the rule "after a prefix, [the *n* of] *hrasva*," the *ṇatva* of *ṇasaḥ* will occur;
by the rule "and [the *n* of] a particle," there is lengthening of the first member;
and by the rule "in a *bahuvrīhi*, [the first member retains its] original form," the first member retains its original accent.
*ratsi* | [derived from] *rada vilekhane* (to scratch), belonging to the *bhūvādi* class.

By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is elision of the suffix *śap*; because it occurs at the beginning of a metrical foot (*pāda*), there is no application of the *aṅ* augment. [The form is] *panthām*.
In the second case singular, [the form is derived] from the rule "ito 'sarvanāmasthāne.
The elision of the letter *n* is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
The acute accent on the first syllable is due to the rule "pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne."

O Agni, you are our wondrous one through your power and the greatness of your skill; in you the divine power has ascended, like a friend worthy of alliance for Kaṇva. 2. You, O Agni, are our wondrous one through your wisdom and the abundance of your strength; in you the asurya-power has mounted, like a friend fit for alliance for Kaṇva. 2.

O Agni, you who are the refuge of all through the excellence of your wondrous power (*adbhuta-sāmarthya*), being pleased by our *kratu*—that is, by our ritual action consisting of our performance of sacrifices and other rites—do grant us, as a supplement, the gift known as *maṃhanā*, which is the act of giving, of strength (*dakṣa*) or of wealth. 1. [Variant readings: *paripāptavyāpanena*] 2. [Variant readings: *āmantritanighātaḥ*] 3. [Variant readings: *tathoktam*] 4. [The manuscripts designated as *jha*, *ta*, *na*, and *ra*]

Because, O *svadhi*, you have ascended (*āruhat*) to the *asurya*—the power of the Asuras—from that cause you are worthy of sacrifice (*yajñiya*), like Mitra or the Sun. Perform acts characterized by the removal of the one-eyed Rākṣasas who destroy the sacrifice. *Amṛta*: The first syllable is acute (*āyudātta*) because it is a vocative. *Kṛtvā*: From the root *ḍukṛñ* (to make). By the rule "kṛñaḥ katuḥ," the suffix *ṛtu* is applied. The letter *k* is for the purpose of prohibiting *guṇa* and *vṛddhi*. There is a *yaṇ*-substitution. *Ṛtu* means action. In the singular instrumental case, by the statement "in *jas* etc., there is optionally [no elision]," there is no absence of the *jā*-elision. *Dakṣasya*: From the root *dakṣ* (to go/to injure). *Dakṣa* is power, because by it enemies are made to flee (*dakṣyante*) or are injured (*hiṃsyante*). By the rule "karaṇādhikaraṇayośca," the suffix *ghañ* is applied. Because it has the indicator *j*, it is acute on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*). *Mahanā*: The root *mahi* has the sense of giving. By the rule "supāṃ suluk," there is the substitution of *ā*. *Tve*: By the rule "supāṃ suluk" etc., there is the substitution of *śeṣa* for the vocative ending *he*. Because it is a substitute for a case-ending (*subādeśatvāt*), it is unaccented (*anudātta*).
O Agni, O radiant one, those men who beautify—that is, make splendid—their words, which take the form of hymns addressed to you, become most prosperous; that is, they become possessed of wealth.
By this, all forms of abundance are indicated.
Furthermore:

Being powerful (*śuṣminaḥ*), they become the witherers of their enemies through their own powers and strengths (*śuṣmabhiḥ*). For those who offer this praise which is free from attachment, even from the great height of heaven (*divaś cit bṛhat*), there arises a vast and excellent fame (*sukīrtiḥ*);
that is to say, their fame pervades the entire expanse of all directions.
Gayadhamaṇa himself, by his own self, awakens—that is, causes you who are such as this to awaken.
*Śubham* means "bright" or "shining. It belongs to the *tudādi* class [of roots]. There is no elision (*lopa*) of the initial syllable due to the application of the rule *pādādi-vāgni-hatābhāvaḥ*.
When the rule for the anudātta accent of sārvadhātuka suffixes would otherwise apply, the accent of the kṛt-suffix (ikaraṇasvara) alone prevails because it is the remaining one. Thus: *aśrārādhasaḥ*.
[The root] *aś* [is used] in the sense of pervasion (*vyāpti*).
The suffix *kan* is applied by the rule “*aśrapuṣi-*” etc.
[Pāṇini 5.2.127]. It is called *aśra* because it traverses (*aśnute*) or pervades (*vyāpnoti*) the path;
it is accented on the first syllable due to the *niṣ* prefix.
The root *rādh* means "to accomplish" or "to perfect. Because one accomplishes or brings to fulfillment dharma and other goals by means of it, wealth is called *rādha*.
Because it is a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accentuation of the first member remains its original form (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*). [The word] *bṛhat*:
from the roots *bṛha* or *bṛhi*, meaning "to grow" (*vṛddhau*).
The suffix *śatṛ* [is present];
the elision of the feminine suffix *ḍīp* is Vedic;
[the word takes] the accent of the suffix.
He understands (*bodhati*). [The root] *budh* means "to understand.

When the suffix *śap* is applied to the causative form (*ṇyantāt*), the designation *sārvadhātuka* applies by the rule "in the Veda, both ways" (*chandasyubhayathā*), resulting in the elision of the *ṇi*.

In the phrase *yadvṛttānnityam*, there is an absence of the *nighāta* (unaccented) tone; it is acutely accented on the first syllable by the accentual rule of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*). [The word] *rmanā*.
The elision of the vowel *ā* [in the word *ātman*] occurs according to the rule: “*mantre vaḍāḍyāderātmanaḥ*” (Pāṇini 6.4.141).
O Agni, those flames of yours go forth boldly,
gleaming like lightning as they spread around, sounding like a chariot seeking the prize.
O Agni, those flames of yours go forth boldly, shining brightly like lightning around the sacrificer; they are like a rattling chariot seeking the prize. 5.
O Agni, those well-known rays of yours—bold, exceedingly confident, and shining brilliantly—go forth everywhere. How so?
Like flashes of lightning, they are pervasive, spreading all around and reaching every direction.
By this, the excellence of their brilliance is expressed.
"Svānaḥ" means resounding; "rathaḥ na" means like a chariot.
By this, the superiority of the sound of the lightning-flashes is expressed.
"Vājayu" means: just as one desiring food proceeds toward battle for the sake of conquering enemies in order to obtain food, so it is here;
by this, the longing directed toward the oblation is expressed.
They go; from the root *iṇ*, meaning "to go.
With boldness.

The root *dhṛṣ* is used in the sense of audacity (*prāgalbhya*). The suffix *ku* is applied by the rule *tramigṛdhṛṣṇi-* etc. (Uṇādi Sūtra). The prohibition of the substitution of *it* is applied by the rule *āditaśca* (Pāṇini 7.2.16).
In the plural, the substitution of *yaj* [for the case ending] occurs by the rule “*supāṃ suluk...*”;
[the word] has an udātta accent on the final syllable by the rule “*citaḥ*”. [Thus: *parijamānaḥ*.

The root *aj* means "to go" or "to move. From the root preceded by the prefix *pari*, the suffix *manin* is applied according to the rule "it is seen after other roots as well," followed by the elision of the vowel *a*.
Chāndasa;
[the suffix] -a is udātta after nis;
[the suffix] -u after vāja.
The suffix *kyac* is applied [to the root *vāja*] in the sense "one who desires vāja for oneself.

By the rule "not in the Veda when [the word] does not end in *putra*," the long vowel (*ī*) and the *vṛddhi* substitution are prohibited. Then, by the rule "after a word ending in *kyac*, the suffix *u* is used in the Veda," the suffix *u* is added.
O Agni, [come] for our protection and for the granting of great wealth;
and may our patrons cross over all regions.
Now, O Agni, for our protection, you who are rich in nourishment, grant us gifts; and may our patrons cross over all regions. 6.
1. śa-°digantarālāvartinī | 2. kha-ca-ṇa-eva śiṣyate | 3. ca-jha-ṇa-bha-ra-śa-aśipuṣi0 | 4. kha-ca-jha-ṇa-na-bha-ra-śa-arciṣaḥ |

O Agni, be with us now for our swift protection and for our preservation. And be present for the granting—that is, the giving—of riches to us who are beset by afflictions, that is, those accompanied by the distress caused by poverty. Furthermore, let our own people—our sons, friends, and so forth—and our praisers, like the sun, be capable of crossing all directions, that is, all quarters; or alternatively, "āśāḥ" means desires. The sense is this: "Fulfill the attainment of all desired and excellent things. Regarding the word *sabādhasaḥ*: from the root *bādh* with the suffix *asun*. That which exists together with *bādhas* (affliction) is *sabādhāḥ*. The form *saha* becomes *sa-* according to the rule *vopasarjanasya*. It bears the accent of the original base of the final member of the compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*). Regarding *rātaye*: from the root *rā* (to give) with the suffix *kin*. By the rule *mantre vṛṣeṣapacamana...* [Pāṇini 3.3.96], it is accented on the final syllable. Regarding *asmākāsaḥ*: when the suffix *aṇ* is applied by the rule *tasminniti ca yuṣmākāsmākau*, the substitution *asmākā-* occurs. Due to the Vedic character (*chāndasatvāt*), there is the elision of *aṇ*. In the plural, the augment *asuk* is added. Since it is observed to be accented on the middle syllable in the genitive plural, the Teacher has likewise made the substitute form so accented. Regarding *viśvāḥ*: from the root *viś* with the suffix *kan* by the rule *aśipruvi...* etc.; it is accented on the first syllable (*ādyudāttaḥ*) because it belongs to the *nipāta* class. Regarding *tarīṣaṇa*: from the roots *tṛ* (to swim/cross), with the suffix *īṣan* by the rule *kṛtyāmīṣan* (Vārttika 4.466). Due to the general rule of abundance (*bahulavacanāt*), there is no elision of the *n*. The final accent is Vedic (*chāndasaḥ*).

O Agni Aṅgiras, you who have been praised and are being praised, bring us wealth that overcomes all, O Hotṛ; for our praisers you are being lauded, and may you increase us in battles through these our prayers.

O Agni, O Aṅgiras, you who have been praised and are being praised, bring to us, O Hotṛ, wealth that overcomes all; for our singers you are being lauded, and may you be present for our increase in battles. 7.
O Agni Aṅgiras!
Because of the metaphorical identification of cause and effect, you—who are the source of the Aṅgirases—are also called "Aṅgiras.

O Aṅgiras, praised by the ancient great seers (*maharṣis*) as *stavānaḥ* (the one being lauded), and being praised even now by those of the present day, you are *vibhvāsaham*, the overcomer of the mighty.
Because it is the cause of overcoming, wealth is called "the overcomer. Bring—that is, fetch—*rayiṃ*, wealth, to us, to our selves.
O *hotṛ*, invoker of the gods, grant to us, the singers, the capacity to praise.
And furthermore, in battles, be present for our increase and prosperity.
*stavānaḥ*:
from the root *ṣṭuñ* in the sense of "praising.
In the *śānac* suffix used for the passive (*karmaṇi*), there is an irregular substitution (*vyatyayena*) of the *śap* suffix, and it is accented on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*).
*vibhv-āsa-ham*. In the *saṃhitā*, the genitive plural *vibhūnām* undergoes the substitution of the vowel *ā* according to the rule *supām* etc.;
furthermore, the genitive case ending is not elided (*aluk*) by the rule *tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam*.

The authors of the *Padapāṭha*, however, considering that [the root] *hu* preceded by *vi-* has the augment *ag* and that lengthening occurs according to the rule "it is seen in other cases as well" (*anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate*), insert the *avagraha*.
There is the original accent of the final member of the *kṛt*-compound.
[The form is] *stavase*.
The root *ṣṭuñ* is used in the sense of praising. The suffix *asen* is applied in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*). It is udātta-accented on its first syllable.

"Janasya gopāḥ" is the eleventh hymn, consisting of six verses. It is the seerical composition of Sutambhara, the descendant of Atri; it is in the Jagatī meter and is addressed to Agni. Thus it is enumerated: "Janasya [has] six; Sutambhara [composed it]; it is in the Jagatī [meter]. Its application is in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra.
‘O Agni, the guardians of the people, seeking the Truth, [approach] you’ (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.13).

1. *kha-ca-ṇa-śa* signifies poverty (*dāridryanimitta*). 2. *kha-ca-jha-ṇa-bha-ra-śa* refers to "our own" (*asmākāḥ*). 3. *kha-ca-ṇa-bha* has the meaning "he did" (*kṛtavān*); *jha-ra* has the meaning "he did" (*kṛtavān*). 4. *kha-ca-jha-ṇa-ta-na-bha-ra* is said to mean "wealth" (*dhana*). 5. *śa* with the augment *agāgama*. (Ṛgveda 2.16)

The watchful guardian of the people has been born, Agni, the very skillful one, for the sake of new-found prosperity. With his face anointed with ghee, he shines brightly and purely for the Bharatas, great and reaching to heaven. janasya | gopāḥ | ajaniṣṭa | jāgṛviḥ | agniḥ | sudakṣaḥ | suvitāya | navyase | ghṛtapratīkaḥ | bṛhatā | divispṛśā | dyumat | vi | bhāti | bharatebhyaḥ | śuciḥ || 1 ||

The protector (*gopāḥ*) of the people, the guardian and preserver (*rakṣitā*), ever-watchful (*jāgṛviḥ*) and always awake, most skillful (*sudakṣaḥ*) and powerful with a strength worthy of praise by all—1—that Agni has been born (*ajaniṣṭa*) for new (*navyase*) and more recent (*navatarāya*) prosperity (*suvitāya*) for the worlds.

With a face of clarified butter, his limbs kindled by ghee, Agni—pure and stainless—is endowed with a vast, great splendor that touches the heavens and reaches the clouds; such as he is, he shines forth and manifests himself for the sake of the *bharata* priests, so that he may possess radiant luster.
Gopāḥ: [derived from] the root *gup* in the sense of "to protect"; the suffix *āya* is applied.
*gopāyate* | [the suffix] *kip* | due to its being subsequent, there is elision of the [augment] *ad* | 2 |

In this case, since the subsequent [rule] applies first, once the elision of *ṛ* has been effected, the elision of *y* would not occur because there is no basis for the application of the *pratyayalakṣaṇa* rule, as the [elided element] depends on a vowel (*varṇa*).
However, due to the indicatory mark (*jñāpaka*) provided by the initial mention of "elision" (*lopa*) in the rule *lopo vyor vali*, the elision of *y* alone takes place.
Furthermore, an operation consisting of an elision (*lopādeśa*) does not possess the status of being a substitute (*sthānivadbhāva*) with respect to the rule prescribing the elision of *y*.
The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
[The word is] *jāgṛviḥ*.
[The root is] *jāgṛ* in the sense of "the cessation of sleep."

The suffix *kin* is applied by the rule "after the roots *gṛdh*, *stṛ*, and *jāgr*, [the suffix] *kin*. Due to the prohibition stated in the rule "there is no [guṇa] substitution for *jāgr* before affixes other than *vic*, *ciṇ*, *ṅi*, and *su*," there is an absence of guṇa.
Because it is marked with *ni*, it is udātta on its first syllable.
*Sudakṣaḥ*: By the rule "ādyudāttaṃ yac chandasi," the first syllable of the final member of the compound is udātta.
*Suvitāya*.
The substitution of *uvaṅ* for the *su* [of *tanū*] occurs by the rule "there is an addition to *tanu* and so forth in the Vedic language" (*tanvādīnāṃ chandasyupasaṃkhyānam*).
The acute accent on the final syllable of the second member of the compound is due to the rule "after a word ending in *suman*, there is *ka*" (*sumānāt kaḥ*).
[This applies to the form] *navyase*.
The suffix *īyasun* is added to the word *nava* in the sense of superiority (*atiśāyana*). The elision of the vowel *ī* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). Then, there is the elision of the final *a*.
The first syllable is udātta.
In the word *divispṛśā*, there is no elision (*aluk*) by virtue of the supplementary rule: "There is an addition [of the prohibition of elision] after *hṛd* and *dyu* before the suffix *cha*."

The word retains the original accent of the final member of the compound (kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam). It contains the suffix *matup*. By the rule "hasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup," the *matup* following a stem ending in a short vowel is udātta at its final syllable.

Men have kindled Agni—the banner of sacrifice, the first appointed priest—in his threefold abode. Together with Indra and the gods on the same chariot, he, the one of excellent wisdom, sits upon the sacrificial grass as the Hotṛ-priest for the performance of the sacrifice. 2. Banner of sacrifice. First. Appointed priest. Agni. Men. In the threefold abode. Together. Kindled. With Indra. With the gods. On the same chariot. He. Upon the sacrificial grass. Sits down. As the Hotṛ. For the sacrifice. Of excellent wisdom. 2.

The men, the priests, first kindled Agni—the banner and indicator of the sacrifice, the one placed at the front by the sacrificers, who shares the same chariot with Indra and the gods—within the *triṣadhastha*, the threefold sacrificial area.
That Agni, the wise one of excellent deeds, the invoker of the gods, sat down upon the *barhis* grass for the sake of the sacrifice; that is to say, he became firmly established there.
*Ketu*:
[derived from] the root *kit* in the sense of "knowledge," with the *uṇ* suffix added according to the *uṇādi* rules.
It has an udātta accent on the final syllable.

In the word *purohitam*, because *puraḥ* is designated as a *gati* by the rule "puro 'vyayam," it receives the original accent of the preceding member (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*) according to the rule "gatiranantaraḥ."
In the three abodes;
by means of this threefold [fire] characterized as the Āhavanīya and so forth. 1. (Variant readings: kha-ca-jha-ṇa-na-ma-ra: praiseworthy).
2. There is elision of the letter *a* because of the following [letters] *kha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *ma*, or *ra*.

3. [The letters] *kha*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *ma*, *ra*, and *na* do not exist [in this context]. That which stands together is *triṣadhasthaḥ*; the suffix *kap* is applied. By the rule "In the Veda, there is the substitution of *sadha* for *saha*" when combined with *māda* or *sthā*, the substitution *sadha* occurs. The accentuation follows the original form of the second member of the compound (*kruduttarapada-prakṛtisvaratvam*). *Sīdat*: From the root *sad*, the substitution *sīd* occurs by the rule beginning with *pā-ghrā-dhām-sthā-mnā-dāṃ śnā* (Pāṇini 7.3.78). The absence of the augment *aṭ* occurs by the rule "In the Veda, [the augment *aṭ* is] frequently absent even when not joined with *mā*" (Pāṇini 6.4.75). There is no violation of the rule regarding the beginning of a quarter-verse (*pādādi*). *Yajathāya*: From the root *yaj*, the *auṇādika* suffix *athap* is added. It is accented on the middle syllable (*madhyodātta*) by the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

Unrubbed, you are born from your two mothers; bright, exhilarating, a seer, you have risen up from Vivasvat. With clarified butter they have strengthened you, O Agni, when you were invoked; your smoke became a banner resting in heaven. Unrubbed, you are born from your two mothers; bright, exhilarating, a seer, you have risen up from Vivasvat. With clarified butter they have strengthened you, O Agni, when you were invoked; your smoke became a banner resting in heaven. 3.

O Agni, from the two parents, the two fire-drills— since they are the cause of your own birth, the fire-drills are also called "parents"— you are born, that is, you manifest, being entirely unpolished and untouched by them.

O *mandra*, praised by all; O *kavi*, who has pervaded everywhere or who is wise; O *śuci*, you arose (*udatiṣṭhaḥ*) from the *vivasvat*, the sacrificer who dwells especially within the house for the sake of the *agnihotra* and other rites. Formerly, the great seers caused you to grow (*avardhayan*), bringing about your increase with clarified butter (*ghṛtena*).
O you who are invoked with oblations, your smoke, offered as oblations, was held in the sky and the intermediate space;
it became the banner, the indicator, because smoke serves as a means of inference.
In the word *mātroḥ*, the accentuation of the case-ending is due to the rule *udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt*. [The word] *mandraḥ* [is formed similarly].
In the phrase *madi stutimodamada-svakāntiṅgatiṣu*,
the word *mada* is derived from the root meaning "to praise" (*stu*) by applying the suffix *rak* according to the rule *sphāyitañci* etc.;
it is udātta on the final syllable.
*Kaviḥ*: From the root *kram*, the suffix *in* is added according to the rule *in sarvadhātubhyaḥ*;
due to the diversity of application (*bāhulakatvāt*), the letter *m* becomes *v* and the letter *r* is elided.
The final udātta accent occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
"Udatiṣṭhaḥ" [is formed from] *tiṣṭhati* preceded by *upa*; there is an absence of the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) because it does not denote an action directed toward oneself (*ahvakarma-vācin*).
From *vivasvat*:
from the root *vas* preceded by the prefix *vi*, the suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) according to the rule for *saṃpad-ādi*;
then the suffix *matup* is added according to the rule “*tad asyāsti*” (it belongs to him).
The substitution of *v* for *m* occurs by the rule "mātṛpadhāyāśca";
because of the *matup* suffix, the word has an anudātta accent, resulting in the udātta accent on the first syllable.

May Agni come straightway to our sacrifice; men carry Agni hither in every house. Agni has become the messenger, the bearer of oblations; choosing him, they choose the one of seer-like wisdom. Agni comes straightway to our sacrifice; men carry Agni hither in every house. Agni has become the messenger, the bearer of oblations; choosing him, they choose the one of seer-like wisdom.
May Agni, the accomplisher of all human goals through his skillful means, come near to our sacrifice;
may he approach. Men carry forth and distribute Agni, the one who bestows grace, from house to house—this is the meaning.
Agni, the bearer of oblations, became the messenger of the gods.
Choosing and honoring him, the virtuous ones choose and honor Agni, who possesses the creative power of a seer and who pervades the sacrifice.
*sādhuyā*: the substitution of *yā* for the case ending is according to the rule *supāṃ suluk* and so forth.

1. From the *ca*-variant; 2. In the *kha*, *ca*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, and *ra* recensions: for the purpose of the *agnihotra*; 3. In the *kha*, *va*, *bha*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *ra* recensions: from *vāsava*; 4. In the *kha*, *va*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *bha*, *ra*, and *śa* recensions: *vin*; 5. In the *ta* recension: by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*). 764. The *Ṛgveda*.
For you, O Agni, let this speech be most honeyed; for you let this inspired thought be a blessing to the heart.
As great rivers fill the ocean with their waters, so do our songs fill you and increase you with power.

To you, O Agni, let this most honeyed speech belong; let this inspired thought be for your heart’s well-being. As great rivers flow toward the ocean, so do these mighty songs fill you with power and cause you to increase. 5.
O Agni, for you—for your sake—this most sweet, exceedingly honeyed speech is being fashioned.
May this inspired thought (manīṣā), which brings peace and happiness to the heart, be for you.
These songs, words in the form of praise, fill you completely.
And they cause him to increase with might and strength. How so?
Like the great, protecting waters (the rivers) [increasing] the ocean, as it were.
O Agni, the Aṅgirases found you hidden in secret, dwelling in every wood; being churned, you are born with great power, and they call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength.
O Agni, the Aṅgirases discovered you, who were hidden in secret, dwelling in every forest; being churned, you are born as great power. They call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength. 6.

O Agni, the Aṅgiras seers found you—hidden in every secret place, placed and concealed in every forest, resting and taking refuge in every tree. Endowed with great and mighty force, being churned, you are born. O Aṅgiras, you who are the archetype of the Aṅgiras, they call you the son of Force (Sahasa). Regarding *śiśriyāṇam*: from the root *śriñ* "to serve" or "to resort to," the suffix *kānac* is applied after the perfect tense (*liṭ*). There is the elision of the *śap* (present marker), and by the rule "śrau," there is reduplication. The substitution of *iyaṅ* occurs; it is accented on the final syllable because of its *cit* designation. 3.
"Prāgnaye ṛtāya" is the twelfth hymn, consisting of six verses; it is composed by Sutambhara, is in the Triṣṭubh meter, and is dedicated to Agni.
It is introduced with the words "Prāgnaye.
This hymn is prescribed for use in the Prātaranuvāka during the Āgneya rite, in the Triṣṭubh meter, and in the Āśvina Śastra.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "To Agni, the great; forward to Agni, the seer" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.13).
I bring forth a prayer toward the ancient, great, and worshipful one, the bull of Truth, the Asura—
like well-poured ghee into the mouth at the sacrifice, I offer this song directed toward the Bull.

To Agni, the great one worthy of sacrifice, the bull of cosmic order (*ṛta*), the Asura—to him I bring this prayer, like well-purified ghee into his mouth at the sacrifice; I offer this song directed toward the Bull. 1.
1. "No," [is said] regarding the *prātaranuvākyā* (morning litany).

To the "Great One" (*bṛhate*)—by virtue of his excellence of power; to the "Worthy of Sacrifice" (*yajñiyāya*), that is, one who is fit for sacrifice; to the "Rain-giver" (*vṛṣṇe*) of "Truth" (*ṛtasya*), that is, of water.
For *ṛta* is listed among the names for water.
To the Asura, the powerful one.
The suffix *uran* is [added] according to the rules of the *uṇādi* group.

I offer forth—a *manman*, a means of knowledge, and a *gir*, a speech in the form of praise—directed toward Agni, the showerer of desires, as one offers clarified butter (*ghṛta*) well-purified and properly consecrated into the mouth [of the fire] at a sacrifice. How so? Just like clarified butter.
The meaning is that the hymn of praise is as pleasing as clarified butter poured into the mouth, which brings delight.
O knower of *ṛta*, take heed of *ṛta*; pierce open the many streams of *ṛta*.
I do not pursue sorcery with force nor through duplicity; I follow the *ṛta* of the wide-striding Bull.

O wise one, take heed of the *ṛta*; indeed, take heed of the *ṛta*. Break open the many streams of the *ṛta*. I do not pursue sorcery by force nor by duplicity; I follow the *ṛta* of the ruddy bull. 2.
O Agni, you who are wise (*cikitvaḥ*), recognize this true hymn (*ṛtam stotram*) being performed by me; know it as the truth (*ṛtam*).
‘Kita jñāne’.
It belongs to the *juhoty-ādi* class.
This is the form in the *lāṅ* (present indicative) tense.
The word *it* is a filler (*pūraṇa*).
Although the word *ṛtam* occurs in the subsequent mantra, due to its Vedic character (*chāndasatva*), it does not undergo the treatment of being like a subsequent member (*parāṅgavadbhāva*).

Furthermore, "open up" (tṛndhi)—that is, pierce through—the many (pūrvīḥ) "streams" (dhārāḥ) of "truth" (ṛtasya), meaning water, in order to produce it for the nourishment of crops, following after the clouds.
Endowed with "force" (sahasā), I "do not touch" (na sapāmi)—meaning I do not contact or, in other words, I do not perform—"the destructive injury" (yātuṃ) caused by ritual action.

The wise and skillful priests, with their mental power—their ritual action consisting of the sacrifice and other rites—place the treasures, the riches, upon the chariot of this Agni, who is wondrous and beautiful to behold. He, Agni, being invoked for the sake of the sacrifice, immediately thereafter is praised among all the clans, among all the people.

1. By means of the excellent [path] of kha, ca, jha, ṇa, na, bha, and ra; 2. It arose from kha, ca, jha, ṇa, ta, na, bha, ra, and śa; 3. Of this wondrous one, from ga, gha, and ja; 4. In kha, ga, dha, ca, ja, jha, ṇa, na, bha, and śa, the word "asya" (of him) is absent.
Truly, let the sun bestow desirable wealth upon us; O Son of Strength, protect us for our aid! Be able to grant us well-being, and stand by us for our increase in battles.
Not so! Nay! For verily the Sun, with his mouth, bestows desirable wealth. O Son of Strength, protect us for our aid; grant us power for our well-being. And be present in battles for our increase. 5.

O Agni, bestow upon us— that is, upon ourselves— now, quickly, desirable wealth that is worthy of being chosen. For indeed, from you, O Sūrya, the singers obtain wealth through their hymns of praise as if through a full mouth.
Furthermore, O *ūrjo napāt*—O son of strength, or O protector of food—grant me food for my desire; this is the sense of the ellipsis.
Protect us; guard us from calamities.
I entreat you: grant us the power for the sake of the security of our mantras and for the preservation of wealth characterized by future prosperity.
By transposition, the middle [person].
Or you become capable; O Agni, moreover, be present for our increase and for the release of the waters in battles and in the midst of hostilities.
The fourth hymn, consisting of five verses, begins with "prātar agniḥ. Regarding this, the table of contents (anukramaṇikā) states: "prātaḥ muktavāhā dvitaḥ.
Thus, the seer (ṛṣi) is Dvita, a descendant of Atri, characterized by the epithet muktavāha.

Regarding the phrase "for it ends in a *paṅkti*," because of the word "hi" (for), the fifth [verse] of this hymn also ends in a *paṅkti*. By the technical rule concerning that which ends in a *paṅkti*, the remaining verses are *anuṣṭubhs*.
The application (*viniyoga*) has been stated for the morning litany (*prātaranuvāka*) and the *āśvina-śastra*.
In the morning, may Agni, the beloved of many, be praised as the guest of the people— he, the immortal one, who delights in all the oblations among those who have prepared them.
In the morning, may Agni, the beloved of many, the guest of the people, be praised—he who, being immortal, delights in all the oblations among those who have minds. 1.
Beloved by many, dear to the multitude, he establishes wealth within the community for the sacrificer.
He is the guest; he is called a *atithi* because he arrives at the houses of the sacrificers like a guest (*atithi*) who comes at an appointed time (*tithi*).
Thus Yāska says: "An *atithi* is so called because he approaches (*abhyaiti*) the house; or because he approaches other families on his way (*tithiṣu*), or other houses" (Nirukta 4.5).
Such an Agni is praised with a morning hymn.
He is the immortal (*amartya*), whose nature is not to die, who takes pleasure in (*raṇayati*) all the oblations (*havyāni*) present among mortals (*mateṣu*), that is, among the human sacrificers.
O you who are borne by two noble steeds, through the greatness of your own skill,
that immortal one places the drop continuously within your heart, even for the praiser.

Twice noble, with his own powerful impulse, he releases the flowing streams; for himself, through the greatness of Dakṣa, he holds the Soma drop in continuous succession—even your praiser, O Immortal One.
1. ma, dha, ja, ya, and cha;
2. kha, ca, jha, ṇa, ta, na, bha, ra, and ā are [the vowels] for the *yajñaiḥ* and *prātarmuktavāhā*.
O Agni, for the one who carries the hymns (*sṛktavāhas*), the son of Dvita (*dvitāya*).
The *sṛktavāh* is so called because it carries—that is, brings to the gods—the pure *sūkta* and the oblation.

For him, O immortal one, be present for the sake of the greatness, that is, the giving, of your own power or wealth. O controller, because that *sṛktavāh* always holds fast to the *indu*, the Soma, for you, the singer indeed becomes a singer.
With a song, I call upon that one of yours who possesses long-lasting luster among the wealthy patrons— those whose chariot, O giver of horses, proceeds unhindered.
Him, whose flame is long-lasting, I invoke for you with a song—him who belongs to the wealthy patrons, whose chariot moves unhindered across the earth, O giver of horses. 3.
O Agni, for the sake of you who possess long-lasting luster and far-reaching radiance—
this plural form is used for honor—
I invoke you with a song, that is, with a hymn of praise, on behalf of the wealthy patrons.
O giver of horses, you bestow horses upon those wealthy men whose chariot, unharmed by enemies in battles, moves forth with its protection gone.
Those in whom there is manifold splendor, who protect with their hymns, for whom the sacred grass is strewn in the light of heaven— these have won renown on every side.
Or those in whom there were brilliant insights, who guard the hymns of praise, and who have placed glorious renown all around upon the strewn sacrificial grass for the Lord of Heaven. 4.
In those officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) among whom there is manifold (*citrá*) and diverse *dīdhiti*— the ritual activity directed toward sacrifice—

who guard (*pānti*) the hymns (*ukthā*) within their mouths, by those priests is the strewn sacrificial grass (*barhis*) overspread; upon that strewn grass, the glories (*śravāṃsi*), the foods, and the oblations are offered to Svarnara—
the sacrifice which leads the sacrificer, the man, to heaven (*sváḥ*).
In him they have placed; they are deposited.
O Agni, for those who have offered fifty dappled horses with common praise, bestow upon them brilliant, great, and lofty renown; drive away the forgetfulness of these wealthy patrons and heroes.
O Agni, for those who have given me fifty horses in joint praise—make their glory radiant, great, and lofty, O immortal one; drive away the [enemies] of these wealthy patrons. 5.

1. [The substitution of *anusvāra* occurs] for *kha*, *ca*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, *ra*, and *dha* when followed by *na*. 2. [The substitution of *anusvāra* occurs] for *kha*, *ca*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, *ra*, and *ga* when followed by *tu*. 3. [The substitution of *anusvāra* occurs] for *ta*, *ra*, *śa*, and *āhṛt* when followed by *īrṇasya*. 4. [The substitution of *anusvāra* occurs] for *ta* when followed by *nidadhire*. 5. [The substitution of *anusvāra* occurs] for *pa*, *pha*, and *ba* when followed by *nidhrīyante*; or [the substitution of *anusvāra* occurs] for the filler (*pūraṇa*).

O Immortal One, those bountiful givers who have bestowed upon me fifty chariots along with praise and immediate well-being—O Foremost One, do thou grant to those generous men a great, vast, and sovereign glory, accompanied by heroes and attendants, and provide them with food. (The sense is: "Grant it! Grant it!")

The fifth hymn, consisting of five verses, begins with "abhyavasthā. Regarding this, the Anukramaṇikā states: "abhyavasthā; Vavri [is the seer]; two [verses] are Gāyatrī, two are Anuṣṭubh, and one is Virāḍ-rūpā.
The seer (ṛṣi) is Vavri of the lineage of Atri.

The first and second verses are in the Gāyatrī meter; the third and fourth are in the Anuṣṭubh meter; and the fifth is in the form of a Virāj, because it possesses the characteristics described in the rule: "That which has eleven syllables in each quarter-verse and eight feet is of the Virāj form."
Abhyavasthā: they are born; he has struck down Vṛtra and poured forth the waters;
he gazes upon them in the lap of his mother.
From the downward place they are born; from the enclosure the chooser has perceived. In the lap of the Mother he gazes abroad. || 1 ||
The wretched conditions—the miserable states—of the seer arise further and further.
May Agni, the distributor of oblations, take notice of such [conditions];
and having understood them, let him be intent on the removal of their state.
That Agni who, being human, beholds—that is, perceives—the multitude of objects situated in the vicinity, in the lap of the earth.
Observing keenly, they have offered oblations; with unblinking eyes, they protect their manly vigor.
They have entered the firm fortress.
Offering oblations, they have become conscious; with unblinking eyes, they protect their manly power. They have entered the firm fortress.

Those people who, discerning and knowing your power, have always offered oblations—invoking you for the sake of sacrifice—and having invoked you, protect and preserve your manly strength with offerings and hymns; they have entered, and continue to enter, your firm citadel, which cannot be overcome by enemies.
As the *Ṛgveda* mantra states: "Protect [us] with a hundred iron fortresses" (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 7.3.7).
The two living beings of Kṣaitreya have increased the splendor of Kr̥tsa; Niṣkagrīva and Bṛhaduktha, seeking booty, [have honored] him with this sweetness as it were.
The people of Kṣaitreya have increased in splendor through the deeds of Kr̥ti; with golden neck-ornaments and great hymns, they are like one seeking booty through this sweet draught. 3.

"Jantavaḥ" means those who are born. "Kṛtvasya" refers to the human officiating priests (*ṛtvij*). With "madhvā na," as if with honey—that is, with this hymn (*stuti*); or rather, the particle "na" has the sense of "ca" (and), meaning "and with honey. And [they have offered] to the son of Kṣetria. "Śvitram" is the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*). To the lightning-fire (*vaidyuta agni*) that exists therein—[the priests] have offered praise. They increase, they cause to grow, the radiant power (*vdyumat*), which is either splendor or strength.
Of what various kinds were they? Their necks were adorned with *niṣkas*—that is, their necks were decorated with gold *niṣkas*.
The singular number is used by way of transposition.
The Bṛhadukthas are those who perform great hymns of praise; the Vājayus are those who desire food.
I milk the beloved, desirable [soma] together with my sisters;
like a cauldron filled with strength, I am undeceived and the constant deceiver.
I win what is dear, milk, and that which is desirable, together with my kinsmen; like a cauldron filled with strength, he is undeceived, eternal, and the subduer of all.

May Agni—he who is associated with Heaven and Earth as their companion, who is like desirable milk that has been milked, who is free from blemish, and who is dear—listen to our beloved hymn of praise.
Of what nature is Agni?
He is like the *gharma* (the Pravargya vessel), possessing a belly full of strength (*vājajaṭhara*).

He whose belly contains *vāja*, which is food, is "one whose belly is *vāja*. Just as *dharma* [the sacrificial fire] is sprinkled with oblations, clarified butter, and milk, so too is he whose belly is the oblation (*havirjaṭhara*).

O Agni, that wealth which you, O best winner of booty, consider most worthy of thought—that wealth, praiseworthy among the gods, do you proclaim for us through our songs as our ally. yam | agne | vājasātam | tvam | cit | manyase | rayim | tam | naḥ | gīrbhiḥ | śravāyyam | devatrā | panaya | yujam || 1 ||

O Agni, O most excellent winner of booty, O you who eat exceedingly, you indeed perceive—*cit* being a filler of the verse—you recognize this wealth, this riches, this oblation-form of wealth being offered by us.

*Śravāyyam*, meaning "worthy of hearing" or "praiseworthy," [is that wealth]; with our hymns (*gīrbhiḥ*), [we offer] that which is joined (*yujam*) to us, our own wealth characterized by the oblation. Bring that, O God, among the gods (*devatrā*)—that is, convey it there.

O Agni, those who do not provoke you—though they have grown great through fierce power—they turn away from hatred and turn away from the wrath of one who follows a different vow. O Agni, those who do not provoke you—though they have grown great through fierce power—they turn away from hatred and turn away from the wrath of one who follows a different vow.

Thus, O possessor of power, for your aid day by day, O wise one, may we be co-sharers in wealth and in the cosmic order; through cattle may we be co-sharers, and through heroic sons may we be co-sharers. Thus, as for your aid, O powerful one, day after day, for the sake of wealth and for the truth, O you of noble intellect, may we be co-sharers in cattle; may we be co-sharers in heroic sons.
O Agni, powerful and mighty one, day after day, every single day, act in such a way that we may be for your protection;
O you of noble wisdom, act so that we may be for wealth, for riches, and for the *ṛta* (the cosmic order) of sacrifice.
Furthermore, may we be those who rejoice together with the cattle.
May we rejoice together with our heroic sons;
act accordingly.
The seventh hymn, consisting of four verses beginning with “manuṣvat tvā,” belongs to Samada, the son of Atri;
this is indicated by the Anukramaṇī: “manuṣvatsasaḥ.
Since it was previously stated that “[the hymns] end in Paṅkti,” these first three hymns conclude with the Paṅkti meter.
The remaining [verses] are in the *anuṣṭubh* meter;
Agni is the deity.
Their application (*viniyoga*) has been stated for the *prātaranuvāka* and the *āśvina-śastra*.

Like Manu, we set thee down; like Manu, we kindle thee. O Agni, O Aṅgiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods. Like Manu, we set thee down; like Manu, we kindle thee. O Agni, O Aṅgiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
O Agni, we establish you, even as Manu did;
the word "manu" is a synonym for "manu."
By the rule "The addition of *vat* [is made] for *aṅgīras* and *manu*," the designation *bha* is applied, resulting in the absence of the short vowel.

Like Manu, let us kindle you with fuel; we shall inflame you with fuel. O Aṅgiras, O Agni whose nature is that of glowing coals, for the sacrificer who desires the gods, sacrifice to the gods like Manu, for the sake of Manu, the offspring of Manu.

For you indeed, O Agni, are kindled among the human folk with great delight; O well-born one, to whom clarified butter is poured, they approach you in succession with beautiful hymns. 2. You; indeed; among the human; folk; O Agni; well-pleased; are kindled; with beautiful praise; to you; they go; in succession; O well-born one; O you to whom clarified butter is poured. 2.
1. In *kha-ca-ma-ṇa-na-ma-ra*, the word "we" (*vayam*) is absent. 2. O fire consisting of burning coals (*aṅgārātmaka*).

Sing forth, O Viśvasāman, like Atri, for him whose flame is purifying—the one who is to be praised at the sacrifices, the Hotṛ priest, most delightful among the people. O Viśvasāman—this is an address to the seer—you, like Atri, sing forth (pra-arca) for that Agni whose flame is purifying (pāvaka-śociṣe). That Agni who, at the sacrifices (adhvareṣu), is to be praised with all songs of praise (īḍyaḥ), the invoker (hotā) of the gods, and who is most delightful (mandratamaḥ) among the people (viśi).

Establish Agni Jātavedas, the divine officiating priest; let the sacrifice proceed in due order, for he is the one who most widely encompasses the gods. O sacrificers, establish Agni Jātavedas—the one whose wisdom is born, or whose wealth is born—the radiant god, the officiating priest who sacrifices at the proper seasons. Let the sacrifice proceed continuously, for he is the one who most extensively provides space for the gods.
O Agni, son of strength (*sahasa*), take note of this service rendered by us and this speech—our hymn of praise; know them well.
O *suśipa*:
one whose jaws (*śipre*) or nostrils are beautiful is called *suśipa*.
This is his address:
O you of beautiful jaws, O slayer of enemies, O lord of the house, O master of the home—Agni’s sons, the fires, magnify you with hymns of praise;
the fires adorn you with songs.

The ninth hymn consists of four verses beginning with “agne sahantam. Regarding this, the Anukramaṇikā states: “agne śugnā viśvacarṣaṇaḥ. Śugnā is the seer (ṛṣi). The fourth verse is a Paṅkti; the first three are Anuṣṭubhs. Agni is the deity. Its application (viniyoga) has been stated because it is included within the nine hymns of the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra.

O Agni, bring hither through the overwhelming power of thy glory a conquering wealth—that which overcomes all peoples by its mouth in the contests for booty. agne sahantam ā bhara dyumnasya prāsahā rayim | viśvā yaścarṣaṇīrabhyāsā vājeṣu sāsahata || 1 || O Agni, bring hither through the overwhelming power of thy glory a conquering wealth—that which overcomes all peoples by its mouth in the contests for booty.
O Agni, bring forth—that is, bestow—upon me, the seer, for the sake of my welfare, great wealth in the form of a son who shall overcome mighty enemies through his innate power.
The genitive case is used in the sense of the dative.

He explains this very point: that son who, being endowed with *āma*—that is, with praise through his mouth—overcomes (*sāmahata*) all (*viśvāḥ*) the people (*carṣaṇīḥ*), meaning all human enemies, as they advance (*abhigatān*) against him in battles (*vājeṣu*).

O Agni, bring that wealth which overcomes hostile armies, O Conqueror! For you, O wondrous Mṛtyu, are the giver of strength consisting of cattle. 2. O Agni, bring that wealth which overcomes hostile armies, O Conqueror! For you, O wondrous Mṛtyu, are the giver of strength consisting of cattle. 2.
O Agni, O powerful one, bring hither—that is, procure—for us a son of wealth who overcomes hostile armies;
for you are the true one, the sustainer of truth, the wonderful, the great, and the giver of food consisting of cattle, joined with kine.

For all people, O most exhilarating one, having trimmed the sacrificial grass, seek you—the beloved Hotṛ-priest—in the sacrificial sessions for many desirable boons. viśve hi tvā sujorṣaso janāso vṛktabarhiṣaḥ | hotāraṃ satrāsu priyaṃ vyanti vāryā puru || 3 || For all people, possessing great vigor, having spread the sacrificial grass, seek you—the beloved Hotṛ-priest—in the sacrificial sessions for many desirable boons.

1. After *ga*, *gha*, *ja*, *śa*, and *ha*, [the suffix] *sahasya* occurs. 2. After *ga*, *gha*, *ja*, and *śa*, the word *ca* does not exist. 3. After *pa*, *pha*, *ba*, and *tvā*, [the suffix] *tām* occurs. 4. After *kha*, *ca*, and *ṇa*, the word *mahyam* does not exist; after *jha*, *bha*, *ra*, and *śa*, [the suffix] *mama* occurs; [and] the word *na* does not exist here. 5. After *jha*, *na*, *bha*, *ra*, and *he*, [the suffix] *sahasvaḥ* occurs.

O Agni, all the people—the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) who have trimmed the sacrificial grass (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*), those who have mown the grass (*lūnabarhiṣaḥ*), and all the others—being of one mind and rejoicing together, in the seven sacrificial halls, seek from you many desirable riches (*vārāṇi*) as they pray to you, the beloved invoker of the gods (*hotāraṃ devānām*).
For he, the protector of all people, has assumed overwhelming power against the malevolent.
O Agni, in these dwellings, shine forth as one rich in wealth, O radiant one; shine forth with splendor, O purifier.
For he, the one who dwells among all people, has indeed assumed power against the assailant. O Agni, in these dwellings, shine richly for us, O bright one; shine with splendor, O purifier! 4.

O Agni, you who are renowned throughout these worlds, the seer (ṛṣi) belonging to all people, may you maintain—hold fast—that conquering power (*sahas*) which destroys the enemies who oppose us. Indeed, *hi* and *ipsa* are particles used for emphasis. O bright and radiant one, shine forth—be kindled—in these our dwellings and homes, so that they may be filled with wealth (*revat*).
O purifying fire, O Agni, shine—be radiant and endowed with glory—upon the sinful ones.
The tenth hymn consists of four verses beginning with “agne tvam naḥ.

Regarding this, the Anukramaṇikā states: “agne tvam: Gaupāyana or Laupāyana, Bandhu, Subandhu, Śrutabandhu, and Viprabandhu; [these] are the authors of the two *dvipadā* verses. These are twenty-syllable *dvipadā-virāj*s.
Because it has been stated thus, those [verses] are the Virāj of two feet.
Subandhu, Śrutabandhu, and Viprabandhu are, respectively, the sages (ṛṣis) of the four [sections];
they belong to the Gaupāyana or Laupāyana lineage.
Agni is the deity.
At the Mahāpitṛyajña, the officiating priests (ṛtvij), proceeding toward the Āhavanīya fire, should mutter this hymn.
Thus it is stated in the Sūtra: ‘Then they approach him, muttering “Mā pragāma” and “agne tvam naḥ”’ (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.19).

On the sixth day of the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*), during the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*), for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest there are two verses beginning with "O Agni, you... (*agne tvam...*) and one verse beginning with "That [you], O most radiant one... (*tat tvā śociṣṭha...*); thus combined, this constitutes the two-pāda *stotriya* hymn.
It is likewise prescribed in the Sūtra: "O Agni, you are our closest [friend]... O Agni, be easy of access through our fuel" (*āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra* 8.2).
O Agni, be our closest relative, our protector, and our auspicious refuge; as a benevolent lord renowned for wealth, come toward us and grant us resplendent riches.
O Agni, be our closest friend, our protector, and our auspicious shelter. As the benevolent Agni, renowned for wealth, come toward us and grant us most resplendent riches. 1. 2.
O Agni, you who provide protection— being worthy of choice and worthy of worship—
or rather,
being protected by the enclosing barriers, become our closest, most intimate friend.
Moreover, O Śiva, be our protector, guardian, and bringer of happiness.
(1) For [the letters] *pa*, *pha*, *ba*, and *ya* are used in the sense of "they beg.
(2) In the manuscripts *kha*, *ca*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, and *ra*, the word ‘*hi...*’ does not exist.
3. Shine with *kha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, and so forth; shine with *ga*, *gha*, *ja*, *śa*, *ḍa*, and so forth. 4.
In the versions *kha*, *ca*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, *ra*, and *ya*, the phrase "and shine endowed with glory" (*yaśoyuktaṃ ca dīdihi*) is absent.
5. In the versions *kha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, and *bha*, the phrase "the *Viṃśatikā* ... or" is absent.

O Vasu, dweller, Agni, leader of all, you who are renowned as wealth (Vasuśravas), come toward us with pervading swiftness; reach out to us! Grant us most radiant wealth, characterized by cattle and other riches; bestow it upon us.
Be mindful of us; hear our call and deliver us from every one who intends us harm. O most radiant, shining one, we now entreat you for the welfare of our friends.
He: Nay! O Agni, hear our call! Deliver us from every one who seeks to harm us. To you, O most radiant and shining one, we now pray for favor for the sake of our friends. 3. 4.
O Agni, as such, be mindful of us; awaken!
Hear our invocation; listen to our call!
From every person who intends us harm, from all such folk, protect us and deliver us.

O most radiant one, O exceedingly luminous Agni, shining with your own splendors—such as you are, you are indeed worthy of praise, whom even the ancient gods kindled as the Hotṛ-priest, the one with the pleasant tongue, the possessor of great light through his brilliant rays. He is indeed the true one, whom even the ancients, even the gods themselves, have kindled—the Hotṛ-priest with the pleasant tongue, the one who possesses abundant light through his brilliant rays.
Even the ancient, most eminent sages [chose] him as the invoker of the gods, the one with the pleasant tongue—
he whose tongue delights the gods through the offering of oblations.
Or rather, he is "one whose tongue gladdens.
Thus Yāska says: "Mandrajihvam means 'having a gladdening tongue' or 'having a tongue that causes joy'" (Nirukta 6.23).

[The gods] kindled—that is, they fully ignited—that Agni, the possessor of light, who is endowed with beautiful splendors (*sudītibhiḥ*). The gods indeed kindled—that is, they fully ignited—that Agni; for that Agni is the Truth (*satya*).
He becomes one whose promise is true;
"from here" is the completion [of the phrase].
With our most excellent prayer and with your most sublime favor,
shine forth for us at the head of wealth;
O Agni, this hymn is being performed for you as the most effective and most capable means of conveyance.
Therefore, O Agni, who art named "the Dispeller of Darkness" (*avibhāvasu*), bestow upon us great and abundant wealth (*bṛhat... dhanam*).
In response to the inquiry as to how this [fire] functions as a giver of wealth, he says:
because from you, from your presence, great wealth (*mahiṣī rayiḥ*) emerges and rises forth.
"Strengths and stones indeed—these rise up, they emerge, from you.
The word "iva" is used as a filler.

Thy brilliant rays resound loudly like the pressing-stone; indeed, thy roar has risen up by itself from heaven like a stretched-out cord. 8. Thy brilliant rays resound loudly like the pressing-stone; indeed, thy roar has risen up by itself from heaven like a stretched-out cord. 8.
O Agni, your rays are indeed brilliant and luminous;
you, the great one, are praised like the pressing-stone at the soma-pressing. And also... [the rest of the verse].

O Purifier, O Cleanser, with your radiant glow and your own splendor; O delightful one, with your tongue which gladdens the gods; O shining Lord, O Agni, bring the gods hither for the sake of the sacrifice, and worship them—perform the sacrifice for them.

We entreat you, O showerer of ghee, O you of wondrous luster, who beholds the light of heaven; bring the gods here for the feast. 2. We entreat you, O showerer of ghee, O you of wondrous luster, who beholds the light of heaven; bring the gods here for the feast. 2.

O you who are dripping with ghee, the impeller of ghee—or rather, born of ghee—O Citrabhānu! [Citrabhānu means] he whose rays (bhānavaḥ) are variegated (citrāḥ), that is, manifold; this is his address. We entreat you, the all-seeing beholder of heaven (svardṛśam); therefore, bring the gods here for the enjoyment (vītaye) of the oblations.

O Sage, we kindle you, the one who accepts the oblation, the radiant one, O Agni, the great one at the sacrifice. 3. O Sage, we kindle you, the one who accepts the oblation, the radiant one, O Agni, the great one at the sacrifice. 3.

O wise Agni, you who possess far-reaching vision, O beloved of the sacrifice, we shall kindle you—who are radiant, blazing, and great—with fuel-sticks at the ritual; we shall inflame you with oblations.

O Agni, come with all the gods for the consumption of the oblation; we choose you as the Hotṛ priest. 4. O Agni! With all the gods! Come! For the eating of the offering! We choose you as the Hotṛ priest. 4.
O Agni, come with all the gods for the sake of the sacrificer who offers the oblation, so that you may partake of the sacrificial offerings;
come toward the sacrifice, since we choose you as the Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods.

O Agni, bring heroic strength to the sacrificer who presses the Soma; sit down with the gods upon the sacred grass. 5. To the sacrificer who presses [the Soma]; hither, O Agni; bring heroic strength; with the gods; sit down; upon the sacred grass. 5.
O Agni, bring and bestow excellent strength (*suvīrya*) upon the sacrificer who presses the soma;
furthermore, sit down together with the gods upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) at the sacrifice.

Being kindled, O Agni, winner of thousands, you nourish the sacred laws; you are the praiseworthy messenger of the gods. 6. Being kindled, O conqueror of thousands, O Agni, you cause the ordinances to flourish; you are the messenger of the gods, worthy of hymns. 6.
1. *kha-ca-ṇa* and *jaritra*; *jha-na-ma-ra* and *jarita*. 2. *pa-pha-ba-taṃ* is like that (*tādṛśam*). 3. *kha-ca-jha-ṇa-ja-ma*—these two belong to *krāntadarśin*.
4. Kha-ra-krāntayajña; jha-krānta-yajña; ta-kāntayajña, or alternatively, priya-yajña.

He is the conqueror of the thousand, the victor over a thousand. O Agni, being kindled with fuel and enkindled with oblations, you, who are worthy of praise and hymns, acting as the messenger of the gods, nourish and sustain our *dharmas*—our ritual acts such as the sacrifice and other ceremonies. Place Agni Jātavedas, the bearer of the oblation, the most youthful, the divine priest, in his station. (7) Place Agni Jātavedas, the bearer of the oblation, the most youthful, the divine priest, in his station. (7)
Those who sacrifice;
[they worship] Jātavedas.
He is called Jātavedas because he knows (vetti) all beings that have been born (jātāni bhūtāni).

Establish, set down, that Agni—the carrier of the *hotṛ*-offering, the bearer of the sacrifice, the youngest, the youthful god, the most excellent invoker, the priest who sacrifices at the proper season.

May the sacrifice proceed today in due order, most spacious for the gods; strew the sacred grass for them to sit upon. 8. May the sacrifice proceed today in succession, most expansive for the gods; strew the sacrificial grass for their seating. 8.

Now, on this day, the sacrifice— most pervaded by the gods, meaning most filled with the shining worshippers— and the oblation which is the means of the sacrifice, [the seer] described through this hymn as the gift of the royal seers Atris before Agni:
"O Vaiśvānara, leader of all men, O Agni, protector of the virtuous, most wise, most renowned, a powerful Asura, a bountiful giver, a possessor of wealth."
The seer is Prathamārya.
Tryaruṇa—the royal seer (rājarṣi) named Tryaruṇa, son of Trivṛṣṇa—gave to me, to my [son], two oxen yoked with a cart (anasvantā), along with ten thousand cows or gold pieces; he gave them to me.
[The root] *mahi* means "to give.
That royal seer was known (*ciketa*) by all people through this act of giving.
O Vaiśvānara, being well-praised and increasing in strength, grant protection in the forefront to Tryaruṇa, who gives me a hundred and twenty cows and two bay horses well-yoked for the chariot.
He who gives me a hundred and twenty cows, and two bay horses well-yoked and easy to harness— O Vaiśvānara Agni, being well-praised and increasing in strength,
grant these to this King Aśvamedha, who, as a seeker and petitioner, impels me toward the bestowing of riches; he thus proclaims, "Give to me!"— that is to say,
he begs for wealth through the horse-sacrifice.
Accompanied by the *ṛc* (verse) and the praise (*stotra*) of Agni, it goes—that is, it approaches—unto him; to that seeker, Aśvamedha gives—that is, bestows—the gift (*sani*) of wealth.
O Agni, to that Aśvamedha who desires the sacrifice (*ṛtāyat*), give—that is, grant—wisdom (*medhā*) concerning the sacrifice.
Whose hundred rough bulls exhilarate me,
like the gifts of Aśvamedha, like Soma-pressings mixed with threefold milk.
Whose hundred rough bulls cause such exhilaration as the gifts of Aśvamedha, like Soma juices mixed with the three-fold milk. || 5 ||
O Agni, may those bulls— givers of the horse-sacrifice, bestowers of coarse yet fulfilling desires, a hundred oxen who gladden me with excellence— may those bulls of yours,
for whom there are three mixtures (consisting of curds, parched barley-flour, and milk) as the means of their preparation,
be like Soma juices for your gratification.
O Indra and Agni, bestow upon Aśvamedha, the giver of a hundred gifts,
great heroic power and a vast dominion that is ageless like the sun in heaven.
O Indra and Agni, bestow upon Aśvamedha a hundredfold gifts, great heroic power, and sovereignty that endures like the unaging sun in heaven. 6.
O Indra and Agni, you two are the givers of hundreds;
that is, you bestow wealth amounting to a hundred upon those who seek it.
In this horse-sacrifice, O Kings, maintain—that is, firmly establish—for us great, vast, and undecaying sovereignty accompanied by excellent heroic power.
How so?
